objective.statement: Optional: rewrite a bar between simple and compound time so that every note keeps its share of its beat.
successCriteria: I know a crotchet beat in simple time becomes a dotted-crotchet beat in compound time.
I give each note and rest the same share of its beat as before.
I beam the new bar as its time signature requires.

explanation.text: The same rhythm can be written in simple or compound time. In 2/4 each beat is a crotchet and divides into two quavers. In 6/8 each beat is a dotted crotchet. If a note takes the whole beat in one, it takes the whole beat in the other, and half a beat stays half a beat. This is optional enrichment: it is not part of the Grade 5 outline and is never assessed.

explanation.caption: 6/8: the same shares of the beat. Every value has gained a dot.

explanation.text: To rewrite from simple to compound time, give every note and rest a dot; to go back, take every dot away. A beat in compound time is a dotted note, so a dot keeps each note's share of the beat. The bar adds up to a different total of note values (six quavers in 6/8 instead of four in 2/4), but it has the same number of beats and lasts just as long. Real compound music usually divides a beat into three quavers; the dotted values used here divide it in two, as duplets do. The pairs are 2/4 and 6/8, 3/4 and 9/8, 4/4 and 12/8. Then beam the notes beat by beat, as the new time signature requires.

steps: Two quavers share the first beat: half a beat each.
In 6/8 half a beat is a dotted quaver.
A crotchet fills a whole beat; in 6/8 that is a dotted crotchet.

feedback.correct: Yes: every note keeps its share of its beat.

mistakes.beam-across-middle: In four-beat bars, keep the two halves of the bar visible — don't beam across the middle.
mistakes.rest-across-beat: That rest hides where a beat begins. Use one rest to finish the beat, and another for the next.
mistakes.half-bar-rest-misplaced: A two-beat rest can fill the first or second half of a four-beat bar, but not the middle two beats.
mistakes.tie-instead-of-dot: A dotted note says the same thing more simply here.
mistakes.compound-beat-hidden: In compound time each beat is a dotted note split into three. Group in threes so each beat shows.
mistakes.values-copied: A beat in compound time is a dotted note, so each value gains a dot (and loses it going back).
mistakes.bar-overfull: Count the beats of the new time signature.
mistakes.bar-underfull: Count the beats of the new time signature.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Mark where each beat starts, then regroup.

recap: Each note and rest keeps its share of its beat.
Simple to compound: add a dot to every value. Compound to simple: take every dot away.
The total of note values changes; the number of beats, and the time the bar lasts, do not.
